findings.title: A spoken claim becomes written liability
findings.claim: The boast's spoken content is written and given an extending punitive consequence in 19:79, then inherited in 19:80; the claimant who expected to receive wealth and offspring instead comes with his words under divine custody.
findings.mechanism: The focus's مَا يَقُولُ repeats the object written in 19:79. Writing fixes the utterance; the adjacent punishment clause gives it an attached consequence; the focus's inheritance verb carries that same speech-object beyond its speaker. The extension wording supports both an added supply and a lengthened term, while its writing contact also permits a bounded ink-supply image.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees the utterance persist as an accountable record whose consequence outlasts the speaker, rather than as a boast that ends when it is spoken.
findings.containment: The focus still says that God inherits what he says and that he comes alone. The writing, judgment, extension, ink, and liability relations are context readings, not extra words in 19:80; the text does not literally name a pen or inkwell. The record-to-inheritance arrow is an inference, and the supplied live alternative is that writing and inheriting are parallel acts.

epistemic.reason: The channel nomination is trusted but first-pass; the exact 19:79-80 surface repetition grounds its writing-to-inheritance contact. The represented HFT trace is legacy_unbound and contributes attributed record, duration, and punishment roles.

findings.title: The expected gift reverses direction
findings.claim: The claimant's forecast that he would be given wealth and offspring is reversed in the focus: God inherits what he said, and he arrives without the promised acquisitions; the wider pericope places this within a return of all beings and their temporary holdings to the Merciful.
findings.mechanism: The context's first-person expectation to receive, with wealth and a child named, meets the focus's inheritance verb and coming-to-Us clause. Later, everyone is described as arriving to the Merciful as a servant and again one by one; this contextual return activates the divine-ownership facet without replacing the focus's direct inheritance claim.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees the line as an answer to the man's own forecast: the expected beneficiary becomes the one dispossessed, and individual arrival belongs to a larger return to divine ownership.
findings.containment: The focus's direct object is مَا يَقُولُ, what he says. Reading the named wealth and offspring as the content of that inheritance is a contextual inference; the supplied live alternative is that only the assertion, not the named goods, is inherited. The later universal-servitude verses do not say that 19:80 lists his entire estate.

epistemic.reason: The claim reversal is the HFT author's explicit inference from exact supplied 19:77 and 19:80 anchors. The added divine-ownership facet is a contextual inference from the supplied servant and universal-arrival statements.
